# dsh-nav-tidy
Hide any panel entry in the **dsh Web** left sidebar — without disabling the plugin behind it.
中文说明
The dsh sidebar lists every installed plugin that registers a global panel. Ten entries in, the list
starts pushing the workspace and session browser down the screen. The official sidebar only offers
a whole-column collapse (56px rail), and the official More menu explicitly does not manage entry vis
ibility, so `dsh-nav-tidy` adds exactly that:

- A **checkbox panel** at the bottom of the sidebar — **More → 侧栏入口…**
- A tiny **console API** (`ds
hNavTidy`) for scripted use
Ticking a row off hides the row. The plugin itself keeps loading and its panel stays reachable; noth
ides the row. The plugin itself keeps loading and its panel stays reachable; nothing is uninstalled.

## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use your own profile name in place of `desktop` (`dsh plugin --profile web add …` for a `dsh web` pr
ofile). Then restart dsh so the client bundle is picked up.
Prebuilt tarball, if you prefer not to build from source:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Use
**Checkbox panel** — sidebar → **More** → **侧栏入口**. Untick a row to hide it, tick it back to restore
; “全部显示” clears the list.
**Nothing is hidden out of the box.** An entry a plugin adds shows up in the sidebar first — hiding
it is your call, not the plugin's.
**Console** — the same store, scriptable:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Matching is **substring, case-insensitive**: `SSH` also hides a row labelled `SSH tunnel`, and `插件`
would also swallow `插件市场`. Rows added by plugins you install later appear in the panel automatically
— no code change needed.
Defaults are persisted under the `dsh-nav-tidy:hidden` key in `localStorage`, so they survive restar
aults are persisted under the `dsh-nav-tidy:hidden` key in `localStorage`, so they survive restarts.
## How it works
1. The panel rows are `<button aria-label="<entry name>">` inside the sidebar root. The plugin tags

that root with `data-nav-tidy-scope`.
2. It injects one stylesheet: `[data-nav-tidy-scope] button[ar

ia-label*="X" i] { display: none !important }`.
3. A `MutationObserver` re-applies the root tag if R
eact replaces the sidebar subtree; a stylesheet means ordinary re-renders need no work.
The checkbox panel is registered into the `sidebar.panellist.actions` list slot — the same seat the
official More menu uses — and renders as a plain DOM overlay, so it does not depend on any component
More menu uses — and renders as a plain DOM overlay, so it does not depend on any component library.
No dsh source is patched, no `@deepseek-ai/*` package is imported at load time. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cl
ient-ui-primitives` is required *optionally* for the menu row (it falls back to a plain button if un
available), and every DOM hook is wrapped in `try/catch`: a failure can cost you the panel, not the
ilable), and every DOM hook is wrapped in `try/catch`: a failure can cost you the panel, not the UI.
## Requirements
- dsh Web (desktop app or `dsh web` profile) with the `sidebar.panellist.actions` slot — present in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` 0.2.2-rc.1 and the builds that ship `dsh-client-ui-entry-custom

ization`.
- Tested against DSH Desktop 0.2.2-rc.1 on Windows.
## Limitations
- **Visual only.** Hidden plugins still load and still consume memory — hide a row here, and disable
the plugin itself if you want the resources back. The plugin collapses the sidebar column natively;

this one manages individual rows.
- Matching is label-based. A row registered without `aria-label`
cannot be targeted; check `[...document.querySelectorAll('nav button')].map(b => b.getAttribute('ari

a-label'))` to see what a row actually exposes.
- The `More` row itself is never hideable — it is th
e way back into the panel.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/index.js` is the host half (an empty `apply` — all work is in the browser), `lib/client.js` is
the browser bundle. The bundle is written directly against the dsh client module contract (`window._
_ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })`), so there is no build step: edit the file and restart dsh.
